footer: Each lesson runs Puzzle → Explore → Name → Challenge (interactive-educator method), for a learner who knows linear algebra, softmax and basic neural networks but is new to NLP. It follows the Pretraining Lab. The deck's history of OpenAI and Alec Radford (slides 1–13) is not turned into lessons. Source decks: M. Samiei, "Lecture 6: GPTs" and "Lecture 5: Pretraining" (slides 96–107), CS 677, Sharif University of Technology (after Radford et al. 2018, 2019; Brown et al. 2020; Holtzman et al. 2020; Lambda 2020). From the slides, reproduced exactly: P(target) .50 .25 .50 .50 .25 .50 and mean cross-entropy 0.924, and the causal mask (Lecture 5 slide 101; slides 19–24); mat 55% / floor 25% / chair 20%, T = 0.5 → 74.7/15.4/9.9% and T = 2 → 43.9/29.6/26.5%, the top-k/top-p distribution 40/25/15/10/6/4% (44–45, 53); the GPT-1 → GPT-2 table, WebText facts, ROUGE 15.03 / 21.40 / 20.98 / 31.55 / 32.75, CoQA F1 27.5 / 45.4 / 54.7 / 55.0 / 66.2 and the 15% overlap / 0.5–1.0 F1 (42–43, 47, 49, 52); the GPT-2 XL and GPT-3 shapes (64); TriviaQA 64.3 / 68.0 / 71.2%, 3-digit addition 34.2 / 65.5 / 80.4% and 5-digit 9.3% (68–69); 2,048 tokens, ≈3.2M per batch, 300B in total, ≈355 V100-years and ≈$4.6M at $1.50/hour (72–73). Derived here: parameter counts from 12·L·d² + V·d, compute from 6·N·D at 28 TFLOP/s per V100, and KV-cache sizes from 2·L·d·tokens·2 bytes. Everything else is a teaching toy: the work counts in lesson 1, the per-token probabilities and decision examples in lesson 2, the n-gram model and its 8 training pages in lesson 3, the second decoding step and the two challenge distributions in lesson 4, the 2-layer attention model in lesson 5, the frozen similarity scorer and its reviews in lesson 6, and the challenge budgets.
